_comment: Phrases that mean the user is stating a STANDING instruction, not making a passing remark. Matched deterministically at the start of a sentence in a user's turn; a hit writes a durable memory immediately and shows an undoable confirmation. Content because this is language, it is tunable, and getting it wrong should cost a PR rather than an App Store cycle.
_added: 2026-09-15 — Lawrence, after scolding an assistant for something it got wrong in a cover letter: 'I asked it to remember to not do that in the future (how does that work? Does that hopefully get stored as a memory somewhere that's durable?)'. It did not, reliably: the only paths were the agent voluntarily calling assistant.remember (measured at 2 memories in 22 hours of real work) and a once-a-day distiller.
_falsePositivePolicy: Be moderately liberal. Every hit is SHOWN to the user and undoable in one click, so a false positive costs a click; a miss costs a correction silently lost, which is what this replaces.
_stoplistComment: Sentences containing these are NOT standing instructions, however they start. 'Never mind' and 'remember when' are the obvious traps; the rest are narrative uses of the same words.
